title: Slow Violence and the Environmentalism of the Poor

vibeProfile.oneLine: How to see the slow, creeping environmental violence that falls on the poor.

summary: Rob Nixon's influential study names 'slow violence', the gradual, out-of-sight damage of pollution, climate change and toxic legacies that falls hardest on the world's poor and unfolds too slowly to make the news. Drawing on writer-activists from across the global South, he asks how art and storytelling can make such creeping catastrophes visible. Rigorous and eloquent, it has become a foundational text in environmental humanities and a powerful argument for the environmentalism of those who suffer harm first and longest.
whyReadIt: The book that named 'slow violence', the creeping environmental harm that hits the poor hardest. Foundational and eloquent.

funFacts.text: The phrase 'slow violence' has become widely used across environmental scholarship and journalism.
